[LG Innotek] 2026 Global Internship (Hiring-Linked) for International Students
As a trusted technology partner and innovation leader transforming industries,
LG Innotek is leading future technological changes in electronics, mobility, and robotics, while realizing customers’ visions together.
We welcome talented individuals who want to change the world with us.
1. Open Positions ( Please refer to the detailed job posting)
2. Eligibility
Applicants who can work full-time in Korea for 5 weeks during July–August 2026
Foreign nationals enrolled in Korean universities as undergraduate students (3rd year or above), master’s/PhD students, or degree holders
(Graduates and those expected to graduate in August 2026 are also eligible)
Holders of TOPIK Level 4–6 (within the 2-year validity period)
Applicants who currently hold or can obtain a valid visa/status for internship participation
3. Preferred Qualifications
Strong language proficiency (business communication level preferred)
Recipients of GKS (Global Korea Scholarship) or those who completed KIIP Level 5
Target languages: English, Vietnamese, Chinese, Spanish, Polish, Indonesian
Preferred language requirements may differ by job category. Please refer to the detailed job posting.
4. Application
Deadline: ~ May 7, 2026 (Thu), 16:00 KST
Job Posting: https://careers.lg.com/apply/detail?id=1001631
Applications must be submitted online via LG Careers only
Final submission deadline is May 7 (Thu), 16:00 Korean Standard Time
Applications can be edited until the deadline after submission

(Internship with Opportunity for Full-Time Return Offer)
Hiring Position
DX Engineer (Front-end / Back-end Engineer)
: DX Engineers leverage their experiences working on projects in various industries and new IT technologies to provide customized services to clients,
while also enhancing the value of clients' businesses. This role will be responsible for a wide range of global IT projects, such as developing, operating,

The Foreign Employment Support Center of the Gyeonggi Job Foundation is recruiting members for the [ Gyeonggi Global Job Supporters (SNS Foreign Employment Ambassadors) ].
Participants will be able to post and promote information related to employment opportunities for foreigners through their own SNS (social media) accounts. The program is open to foreign residents in Korea.
- Recruitment Period: March 4, 2026 – March 25, 2026
- Eligibility: Foreign residents legally staying in Korea with a valid visa, especially those who manage influential communities or SNS accounts.
- Activities: Posting SNS content related to foreign employment at least once a week, Participating in related events
- Benefits: Activity allowance (e.g., attendance stipend), SNS-related training, Rewards for outstanding participants, Certificate of appointment
- Application Method: Apply online via Jobaba Apply( https://apply.jobaba.net/bsns/bsnsDetailView.do?bsnsSeq=5320) (or scan the QR code on the poster)
- Details: Please refer to the poster for more information.

HY-in log in  Application  Leave of Absence  Upload a copy of passport

■ Cautions
① Those who apply for the leave of absence must leave Korea within one month,
regardless of their visa validity periods.
② Universities are required to report the list of students who take a leave of absence
or are not attending school to the Immigration Office each semester. Students who
stay in Korea without attending school are subject to fines from the Immigration
Office.
③ When you go back to your country after taking a leave of absence, you have to
return your alien registration card at the airport.
④ Students who stay and work in Korea illegally while on leave of absence might have
disadvantages when returning to the school.
⑤ Students who pay tuition and take leave of absence, can’t get tuition refunds.
Tuition will be carried over to next semester.

The Department of Media Communication (formerly the Department of Journalism & Mass
Communication) examines diverse media and communication phenomena in contemporary society.
Media communication studies represent an interdisciplinary convergence point, integrating multiple
social sciences, including sociology, psychology, economics, political science, and information science.
Communication, encompassing expressing and transmitting thoughts and feelings through verbal,
written, and symbolic means, is a fundamental component of societal function. As noted by Peter
Drucker, “self-expression represents a critical human capability, with modern business and management
fundamentally dependent on communication competency.” Communication proficiency proves essential
across professional effectiveness, interpersonal relationships, persuasive discourse, and personal
development. Media serves as the primary vehicle for this communication process. The contemporary
media landscape demonstrates rapid evolution, advancing beyond traditional channels such as
correspondence, print journalism, radio, and television. Digital platforms, including internet applications,
interactive gaming, and social media networks accessed through computers and mobile devices, reflect
increasing technological sophistication in modern communication systems.
Contemporary society demonstrates extensive integration with media systems. Individual citizens,
commercial enterprises, and governmental institutions utilize diverse media platforms and artificial
intelligence tools, creating widespread societal impact. The Department of Media Communication
develops professionals with advanced communication capabilities and media literacy skills aligned with
contemporary societal requirements.
